correctness.rationale: One iteration satisfies x_new-y_new=2max(-x,0)+2a max(y,0)>=0. The invariant negative cone y<=x<=0 has affine matrix [-1,a;1,a] and both eigenvalues outside [-1,1], with affine fixed point outside cone; hence strong divergence there. Positive cone x>=y>=0 has expanding invertible matrix [1,a;1,-a] with unique fixed P=(2+1/a,1/a). In fourth quadrant x>=0>=y the map collapses to (t,t), t=x+ay-1; the remaining positive diagonal excursions return via t->(1+2a-a²)t-(a+2). If a>=2 returns descend into negative cone; if 1<=a<2 the sole fixed return is q=(a+2)/(a(2-a)), below q enters negative cone and above q diverges, with q forming the cycle. Backward preimages of special orbits are countably many affine lines/points owing to the rank-one branch; hence planar null. I independently checked the eigenvalue polynomial signs at ±1 and two-step return algebra, including a=1 and 2 endpoints; numerical simulations alone would be insufficient.
